thread:
emily: customer asked for a declarative way to enforce upgrade windows + bandwidth caps + blackout windows on their on-prem clusters. they want it in config, not a manual opt-out.
owen: can we do policy-as-code embedded in the manifest? makes it portable with the bundle, and operators can validate before apply.
nikhil: big +1 but be careful: some customers want org-level policies that override per-manifest hints. need precedence rules.
claire: proposed model: 1) manifest may include an optional `upgrade_policy` block; 2) operator has a per-cluster policy store; 3) effective policy = merge(cluster policy, manifest policy) with cluster policy taking precedence. keep merge simple (last-wins) and document conflict rules.
maria: what are the policy knobs we want initially? my list: blackout_windows, allowed_weekdays, max_concurrent_upgrades, bandwidth_limit_bytes_per_minute, preflight_hook (exec image), drain_strategy, require_manual_approval_for_major, schema_version.
emily: agree. also need simulation mode and dry-run flag so customers can see what an upgrade would have done without applying.
owen: here's a compact example we can use in RFC: 
```yaml
upgrade_policy:
  schema: v1
  blackout_windows:
    - start: "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z"
      end: "2026-04-02T06:00:00Z"
      reason: maintenance
  allowed_weekdays: [mon,tue,wed,thu,fri]
  max_concurrent_upgrades: 2
  bandwidth_limit_bytes_per_minute: 10485760 # 10MB/min
  preflight_hook:
    image: registry.internal/preflight-check:1.2.0
    timeout_seconds: 300
  drain_strategy: graceful
  require_manual_approval_for_major: true
```
nikhil: love the example. implementation notes: operator should enforce `bandwidth_limit_bytes_per_minute` with a token-bucket per-cluster or per-operator-peer. tokens refill once per minute. streaming patchlets should observe tokens before sending.
claire: admission flow sketch: hub sends manifest+policy -> operator validates effective policy -> if inside blackout window -> reject with 403 and reason; if exceeds concurrency -> queue with ETA; if preflight_hook present -> run hook as a local job, fail-fast on non-zero code. only after all checks pass transition to `scheduled` -> `draining` -> `applying`.
emily: need state machine states visible in console: queued, scheduled, draining, applying, verifying, applied, failed, blocked-by-policy.
own: UX: console should show next-possible-apply-time when blocked by blackout or concurrency. also let SREs request a temporary policy override with an audit comment. overrides should be scoped and expire.
maria: security: override path must be RBAC-gated and emit audit event including who, reason, expiry. also store the override in the cluster audit log.
nikhil: testing: e2e harness should simulate N clusters with varying policies and measure that policy enforcement reduces simultaneous upgrades to <= max_concurrent_upgrades and that bandwidth token-bucket holds under heavy push. add chaos test where preflight hook sometimes times out.
claire: metric set: upgrades_in_progress, upgrades_queued, policy_violations_attempts, overrides_issued, preflight_hook_failures, bandwidth_tokens_exhausted. add alert: if overrides_issued > 5 in 1h page sig-ops.
emily: backward compat: if manifest lacks upgrade_policy, treat as permissive unless cluster policy restricts. schema v1 must be explicit in manifest to avoid silent misinterpretation.
own: storage: cluster policy store should be simple CRD-like object in operator, and hub can push recommended policy via admin API. ensure we support per-namespace and per-cluster scoping.
maria: concerning signer rotation: policy changes that arrive unsigned by old signer must be rejectable; we should require policy updates be signed similar to manifests or come over control-plane channel authenticated to the hub.
nikhil: edge-case: what about networks with extremely low bandwidth where even token-bucket backoff causes long queues? proposal: allow `allow_small_patchlets_during_blackout: true` which permits micro security fixes to pass through when flagged `security_critical = true`. this must be tightly auditable.
emily: runbook notes: when a site reports stuck upgrades: 1) check effective policy; 2) inspect queued items and preflight logs; 3) if override needed, create timeboxed override with justification; 4) monitor post-apply for regressions.
own: API proposal (POST snippet):
```http
POST /operator/apply-request
{
  "manifest_seq": 1234,
  "policy_override": { "expires_at": "2026-04-02T03:00:00Z", "reason": "CVE-xxxx emergency", "actor": "oncall@redwood" },
  "dry_run": false
}
```
claire: console: show a "simulate policy" button that computes earliest apply time and lists which checks will run. helpful for customers to tune policies.
maria: compliance: audit logs should retain policy decisions for 365 days by default. we already have retention tiers but call out this use.
nikhil: perf: merging policies must be inexpensive; implement on the operator with simple JSON merge and cache effective policy per-manifest-seq for X minutes.
emily: volunteers: i'll draft RFC with diagrams (policy merge, state machine, token-bucket), owen will prototype operator hooks, nikhil writes e2e scenarios, claire sketches console, maria writes security/ops appendix.
deploy-bot: policy-service v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-22T14:12Z :white_check_mark:
emily: thanks everyone. i'll file RFC and tag you all. please add comments if you see any missing policy knobs or dangerous default behaviors.
